extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians and computational algebra researchers) who use or implement library procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (Appendix D entries) describing syntax, expected argument types, return types, purpose, assumptions and examples for functions such as modJanet, rwalk family, and multiple procedures in schubert.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: modJanet
rubrics_metrics.description: modJanet(I,i); I is an ideal, i an integer (optional). Returns: ideal, a Janet basis for I using modular methods. If second argument is 0 then the result is not verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: Computes a Janet basis for the ideal given by generators in I using modular techniques. Usage examples show loading rstandard.lib, defining rings and ideals, calling modJanet(i) or modJanet(i,0) and printing the resulting ideal and lengths. Example outputs show lengths and basis elements. Note: second argument controls verification (0 disables verification).

rubrics_metrics.name: prwalk
rubrics_metrics.description: prwalk(I,radius,o_perturb_deg,t_perturb_deg) from rwalk.lib. Type: ideal. Purpose: compute the standard basis of the ideal via the Random Perturbation Walk algorithm from one ordering to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax variants: rwalk(ideal i,int radius) or rwalk(ideal i,int radius,intvec v,intvec w). Example shows computing a Groebner basis w.r.t. lp, specifying radius and perturbation degrees. Outputs illustrate returned basis polynomials. Guidance: use when converting between monomial orderings via perturbation walk algorithm; intermediate outputs shown in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: rwalk
rubrics_metrics.description: rwalk(ideal i, int radius[, intvec v, intvec w]) from rwalk.lib. Type: ideal. Purpose: compute the standard basis of the ideal via the Random Walk algorithm between specified orderings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If size(#)>0 variants accept intvec v and w. Note: intermediate Groebner bases are not reduced if reduction = 0. Example shows calling rwalk with radius and perturbation degree and printing returned basis elements. Use for ordering conversion using random walk.

rubrics_metrics.name: frandwalk
rubrics_metrics.description: frandwalk(ideal i, int radius[, intvec v, intvec w]) (also frandwalk alias in docs) — Random Fractal Walk algorithm to compute standard basis w.r.t. lexicographical or weighted-lex orderings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: frwalk(ideal i,int radius) or frwalk(ideal i,int radius,intvec v,intvec w). Example demonstrates computing a standard basis for lex ordering and shows resulting basis polynomials. Use when lex or weighted lex targets are needed; supports reduction parameter in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeVariety
rubrics_metrics.description: makeVariety(d,i); d int, i ideal. Return: variety. Assume d is a nonnegative integer, i is an ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: create an abstract variety represented by dimension d and a graded ring as its Chow ring (quotient by provided relations). Example demonstrates LIB 'schubert.lib', ring setup and makeVariety(2,rels) returning a variety with .dimension and .relations accessible. Use when building abstract variety objects whose Chow ring equals quotient by given rels.

rubrics_metrics.name: printVariety
rubrics_metrics.description: printVariety(V); V variety. Return: prints/represents an abstract variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the print function used by Singular to display a variety. Example shows calling V where V was created by makeVariety and getting 'A variety of dimension 2'. No other side effects described.

rubrics_metrics.name: productVariety
rubrics_metrics.description: productVariety(U,V); U variety, V variety. Return: variety representing the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: two abstract varieties. Output: product variety whose dimension equals sum of dimensions. Example shows creating projectiveSpace(3) and Grassmannian(2,4) then productVariety(P,G) producing a variety with relations combined; shows accessing baseRing and relations. Use to compute product varieties and their Chow ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: ChowRing
rubrics_metrics.description: ChowRing(V); V variety. Return: qring (the Chow ring as quotient ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes V is an abstract variety. Example shows calling ChowRing(V) printing ring metadata (coefficients QQ, number of vars, orderings, variable names). Use to obtain the underlying quotient ring representing the variety's Chow ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grassmannian
rubrics_metrics.description: Grassmannian(k,n); k int, n int. Return: variety representing G(k,n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates Grassmannian G(k,n) as abstract variety with dimension k(n-k) and Chow ring quotient of polynomial ring in n-k variables q(1..n-k) (Chern classes). Monomial ordering 'wp' used with vector (1..k,1..n-k). Exports Chern characters of tautological subbundle and quotient bundle. Example G(2,4) shows dimension, relations, exported subBundle and quotientBundle polynomials. Use for standard Grassmannians and to obtain Chern data and relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: projectiveSpace
rubrics_metrics.description: projectiveSpace(n); n int. Return: variety representing projective space of dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: quotient ring in one variable h modulo ideal generated by h^(n+1). Example shows P=projectiveSpace(3) with .relations containing h4 and ChowRing showing ring metadata. Use to model projective spaces and obtain standard relation h^(n+1)=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: projectiveBundle
rubrics_metrics.description: projectiveBundle(S); S sheaf. Return: variety — the projective bundle associated to sheaf S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: a sheaf on an abstract variety. Purpose: create projective bundle variety (used in enumeration of conics). Example constructs sheaf, dualSheaf powers, then projectiveBundle to obtain PB with dimension and QuotientBundle polynomial; shows querying ChowRing(PB). Use when constructing projective bundles of sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: integral
rubrics_metrics.description: integral(V,f); V variety, f poly. Return: int. Purpose: computing intersection numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: abstract variety V and polynomial f in its Chow ring. Example: integral(Grassmannian(2,4), q(1)^4) returns 2. Use to compute intersection numbers (integration of top-degree classes).

rubrics_metrics.name: makeSheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: makeSheaf(V,ch); V variety, ch poly. Return: sheaf. Theory: create a sheaf on an abstract variety with Chern character ch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs variety X with baseRing, defines c and ch, calls makeSheaf(X,ch) and inspects returned sheaf (e.g., rank). Use when building sheaves with a given Chern character for later operations (Chern classes, tensor, dual, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: printSheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: printSheaf(S); S sheaf. Return: string / standard printed representation of sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Singular print function for sheaves. Example demonstrates printing a sheaf created by makeSheaf which prints 'A sheaf of rank 2'.

rubrics_metrics.name: rankSheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: rankSheaf(S); S sheaf. Return: int — the rank of a sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: a sheaf S. Example: for sheaf made from makeSheaf(G,subBundle) rankSheaf(S) returns 2. Use to query sheaf rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: totalChernClass
rubrics_metrics.description: totalChernClass(S); S sheaf. Return: poly — the total Chern class of a sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: a sheaf S. Example constructs a sheaf E and S=E^3 then totalChernClass(S) returns explicit polynomial. Use to compute total Chern class for further intersection computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ChernClass
rubrics_metrics.description: ChernClass(S,i); S sheaf, i int. Return: poly — the i-th Chern class of sheaf S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S must be a sheaf, i a nonnegative integer. Example shows ChernClass(S,1..4) returning successive polynomials. Use for extracting individual Chern classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: topChernClass
rubrics_metrics.description: topChernClass(S); S sheaf. Return: poly — the top Chern class of a sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: sheaf S. Example: for B = S^3 where S = makeSheaf(G,quotientBundle), topChernClass(B) returns 27*q(2)^2. Use to get top-degree Chern class for integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: totalSegreClass
rubrics_metrics.description: totalSegreClass(S); S sheaf. Return: poly — the total Segre class of a sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This computes the total Segre class; documentation references totalChernClass. Example shows totalSegreClass(subBundle) returning q(2)+q(1)+1. Use as the Segre analogue of Chern classes in intersection computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: dualSheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: dualSheaf(S); S sheaf. Return: sheaf — the dual of a sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: returns dual sheaf object. Example: for S = makeSheaf(G,subBundle), dualSheaf(S) returns a sheaf of same rank. Related functions: addSheaf, quotSheaf, symmetricPowerSheaf, tensorSheaf. Use to form duals for further sheaf algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: tensorSheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: tensorSheaf(A,B) or A*B; A sheaf, B sheaf. Return: sheaf — the tensor product of two sheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs S and Q and computes T = S*Q returning a sheaf (rank shown). Use to compute tensor products and then compute Chern characters/classes on result.

rubrics_metrics.name: symmetricPowerSheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: symmetricPowerSheaf(S,n); S sheaf, n int. Return: sheaf — the n-th symmetric power of S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: returns symmetric power; example compares symmetricPowerSheaf(S,3) with S^3 and verifies equal ChernCharacter. Use when needing symmetric powers of sheaves while preserving Chern character relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: quotSheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: quotSheaf(A,B); A sheaf, B sheaf. Return: sheaf — the quotient of two sheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs multiple sheaves (dualSheaf powers), projectiveBundle and QuotientBundle then uses quotSheaf to form quotient sheaf A = B5 - V; result is a sheaf object with rank. Use to represent quotient sheaves in constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: addSheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: addSheaf(A,B) or A + B; A sheaf, B sheaf. Return: sheaf — direct sum of two sheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: direct sum. Example shows S+Q with rank and checks ChernCharacter and totalChernClass equivalences. Use to build direct sums and verify relationships among Chern invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeGraphVE
rubrics_metrics.description: makeGraphVE(v,e) where v is a list of vertices and e is a list of edges. Return: graph with specified vertices and edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: creates a graph object from lists. Example: makeGraphVE(list(list(0,1,list(0,1,2)),...), list(list(0,1,2))) returns graph with vertex and edge counts printable. Use when representing combinatorial graphs used in moduli/fixed-point enumerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: printGraphG
rubrics_metrics.description: printGraphG(G); G graph. Prints representation of a graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the print function for graph objects. Example shows calling G and receiving 'A graph with 2 vertices and 1 edges'. Use for human-readable output of graph objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: moduliSpace
rubrics_metrics.description: moduliSpace(V,d); V variety, d int. Assume V is a projective space and d is a positive integer. Return: stack representing moduli space of stable maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: create moduli space of stable maps from genus zero curve to projective space. Example: moduliSpace(projectiveSpace(4),2) returns a stack with dimension 11. Use to build moduli spaces for Gromov-Witten type computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: printStack
rubrics_metrics.description: printStack(M); M stack. Prints a moduli space (stack) representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume M is a moduli space of stable maps. Example yields 'A moduli space of dimension 11'. Use for displaying stack objects produced by moduliSpace.

rubrics_metrics.name: dimStack
rubrics_metrics.description: dimStack(M); M stack. Return: int — the dimension of the moduli space (stack).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: M moduli space of stable maps. Example dimStack(M) returns 11 for moduliSpace(P,2). Use to query expected dimension for intersection computations and fixed point sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: fixedPoints
rubrics_metrics.description: fixedPoints(M); M stack. Return: list of graphs corresponding to fixed point components of torus action on moduli space of stable maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: M moduli space of stable maps. Output: list where each element is a list with a graph and integer(s). Example: fixedPoints(M) returns list of size 100; type checks show elements are lists and first element is a graph. Use to enumerate fixed components required for localization formulas in intersection/Gromov-Witten computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: contributionBundle
rubrics_metrics.description: contributionBundle(M,G,#); M stack, G graph, # list (optional). Return: number corresponding to the contribution bundle on moduli space at the fixed point component (graph).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: moduli space M, graph G, optional list argument. Example: contributionBundle(M,G) and contributionBundle(M,G,5) produce same numeric result; used in Bott localization to get contribution numbers for each fixed component. Use when assembling total intersection/Gromov-Witten invariants by summing contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalBundle
rubrics_metrics.description: normalBundle(M,G); M stack, G graph. Return: number (documented but full text truncated in chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose (implied): compute the normal bundle/its contribution at a fixed point component (graph) for the moduli space M. Related to contributionBundle and fixedPoints; used in localization computations. Example context and further details appear in nearby documentation.
